text:
📢Hiring Data Engineers!

If you can solve these Data Engineering interview questions — you’re the right fit.

🔥 Data Engineer Interview Questions 

1. What is the difference between batch processing and stream processing?
2. Explain how you would design a scalable data pipeline for millions of daily records.
3. How do you handle schema evolution in a data lake?
4. Describe how partitioning and bucketing impact performance in big data systems.
5. What is data skew in Spark, and how do you fix it?
6. Explain the difference between repartition and coalesce in PySpark.
7. How would you optimize a Spark job that is running for several hours?
8. What is the role of the driver and executors in Spark?
9. Explain the concept of idempotency in ETL pipelines.
10. How do you design incremental data loads (CDC) in a Delta Lake pipeline?
11. What is the difference between Parquet, Avro, and ORC file formats?
12. How do you implement data quality checks in production pipelines?
13. Explain how Kafka partitions help in scaling consumers.
14. What are watermarks in streaming pipelines, and why are they required?
15. How do you identify and resolve performance bottlenecks in SQL queries?
16. Describe star schema and snowflake schema with use cases.
17. What are Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD), and when do you use them?
18. How do you secure a cloud data pipeline (IAM roles, encryption, VPC)?
19. What is a feature store, and why is it needed in ML systems?
20. Explain the differences between OLTP and OLAP architectures.

text:
Stop writing subqueries for deduplication

There's a better way

Every data engineer has written that nested query with ROW_NUMBER( ) and a WHERE clause.

It works. But it's ugly.

QUALIFY does the same thing in one line

No subquery. No CTE. Just clean SQL.

It flters window functions directly - like WHERE does for rows and HAVING does for aggregates.

Works in : -
-> Snowflake 
-> BigQuery 
-> Databricks SOL

I use this daily for : 
-> Getting the latest record per customer 
-> Removing duplicate events 
-> Finding the first purchase per user

One line that saves 5 lines of nesting

author: Omkar Sonawane
headline: Senior Data & AI Engineer | Top 1% on TopMate | 5 years of experience | Expert in PySpark AWS SQL Python Kafka
text:
Don’t 𝗗𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗡𝗖𝗧 every time to remove duplicates in SQL.

There are 5 other method you choose should match your intent:
Quick audit? Use aggregation.
Clean deletion? Use window functions.
Root cause analysis? Use self-joins.
Preserving the "right" record? Use conditional logic.
Cross-table validation? Use EXISTS.

Here are 5 battle-tested ways to find (and handle) duplicates in SQL:
1️⃣ 𝗚𝗥𝗢𝗨𝗣 𝗕𝗬 + 𝗛𝗔𝗩𝗜𝗡𝗚 → 
Your go-to for getting the lay of the land. Shows you which keys are duplicated and how many times. 
Fast, simple, diagnostic.

2️⃣ 𝗥𝗢𝗪_𝗡𝗨𝗠𝗕𝗘𝗥() → 
Precision tool for deduplication. Ranks each occurrence so you can surgically remove extras (WHERE rn > 1) or keep the first/last based on criteria.

3️⃣ 𝗦𝗘𝗟𝗙 𝗝𝗢𝗜𝗡 → 
When you need to see duplicates side-by-side. 
Perfect for comparing conflicting values across duplicate rows and understanding why they're duplicates.

4️⃣ 𝗗𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗡𝗖𝗧 + 𝗡𝗢𝗧 𝗜𝗡/𝗘𝗫𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗦 → 
Identifies records that appear in one table but shouldn't duplicate in another. 
Great for cross-table integrity checks and referential cleanup.

5️⃣ 𝗣𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗜𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗕𝗬 (𝗠𝘂𝗹𝘁𝗶𝗽𝗹𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗹𝘂𝗺𝗻𝘀) → 
Finds duplicates within specific segments. 
Example: same customer name within each city, but different cities can have same names. Adds nuance to your deduplication logic.

⚡️🗓️ 𝗧𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝟭𝟴𝘁𝗵 𝗝𝗮𝗻𝘂𝗮𝗿𝘆 (𝗦𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗮𝘆), I'm hosting our 3rd webinar which will prepare you to crack and prepare 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗘𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄𝘀 (14/𝟰𝟬 𝗦𝗲𝗮𝘁𝘀 𝗹𝗲𝗳𝘁) 𝗟𝗶𝗻𝗸 𝗶𝗻 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 👇

text:
While switching from Accenture, I interviewed at Tiger Analytics for a Data Engineer role (19 LPA).

So, sharing below my interview experience, hope it helps 🤞

The whole interview process had 3 rounds.

📍ROUND 1: Big data, coding
The round started with a general introduction, questions around my project experience & tech stack, and then:

1.⁠ ⁠Write a SQL query to find duplicate records in a table.
2.⁠ ⁠How would you perform a join on very large datasets?
3.⁠ ⁠What types of joins would you avoid for performance reasons?
4.⁠ ⁠How do you process large CSV file without running to memory issues?
5.⁠ ⁠How do you optimize Spark jobs?
6.⁠ ⁠Explain partitioning and bucketing in Hive and their use cases.
7.⁠ ⁠What was your experience with desinging scalable and efficient data pipelines?
8.⁠ ⁠Calculate the total sales per customer and per product category on sales data using pyspark
9.⁠ ⁠CI/CD experience, couple of python questions as well

📍ROUND 2: Advanced big data, real time
This round too started with a discussion around my Project experience, and then→ 
1.⁠ ⁠How would you ensure data consistency and reliability in a distributed system?
2.⁠ ⁠How would you improve the performance of a slow-running ETL job?
3.⁠ ⁠Explain your experience with Cloud? explain the services used in Azure?
4.⁠ ⁠Explain your experience with ADF, activities used? how did you optimize the pipeline?
5.⁠ ⁠Explain your experience with Star schema, data warehousing expereince?
6.⁠ ⁠Explain the spark streaming experience?
7.⁠ ⁠In depth questions on CI/CD pipelines, what was your tools used to deploy code?
8.⁠ ⁠More questions on scenario based questions, around azure cloud.

author: Gunja Singh
headline: Data Engineer | 5+ Years Experience | ETL, Big Data, Cloud (AWS | Azure | GCP) | SQL | Python | Spark
text:
🚀 Data Engineer Interviews in 2026 are NOT about tools anymore.
Sunday reality check 👇
Last week, I reviewed 12 Data Engineer resumes.
All had:
✅ Spark
 ✅ SQL
 ✅ Python
 ✅ AWS / Azure
 ✅ Airflow
Yet…
8 failed the technical round.
Not because they were weak.
But because they prepared for 2025 interviews.
Here’s what actually decides selection in 2026 👇
1️⃣ Data Modeling for Analytics (Not just tables)
Interviewers care about:
• Star vs Snowflake
 • Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD)
 • Fact table grain
 • Query patterns
 • BI performance
Not just:
“I know normalization.”
2️⃣ Real SQL (not LeetCode SQL)
They test:
• Window functions
 • Query optimization
 • Execution plans
 • Handling skewed data
 • Incremental loads
 • Dedup logic
If your SQL is weak → pipeline is weak.
3️⃣ Spark Internals (not just APIs)
Know:
• Shuffle
 • Partitioning
 • Broadcast joins
 • Memory management
 • Wide vs narrow transformations
 • Why jobs become slow
This separates junior from senior.
4️⃣ Data Pipeline Design
They expect you to explain:
• Batch vs streaming
 • Idempotency
 • Late arriving data
 • Schema evolution
 • Failure recovery
 • Backfilling strategy
Real systems break.
 Your design must survive it.
5️⃣ Cloud Architecture
Not:
“I used S3.”
But:
• Lakehouse vs Data Warehouse
 • Storage formats (Parquet / Delta / Iceberg)
 • Cost optimization
 • Security (IAM, VPC, private endpoints)
 • Cross-region strategy
6️⃣ Data Quality & Observability
New focus in 2026:
• Data validation checks
 • Null drift
 • Volume anomalies
 • Freshness SLAs
 • Monitoring pipelines
 • Alerting strategy
Broken data = broken business.
7️⃣ System Design for Data
They will ask:
“Design Uber’s data pipeline.”
They mean:
• Ingestion
 • Streaming layer
 • Storage
 • Processing
 • Serving layer
 • BI consumption
